from_quote: confiding the ultimate right of regulating its own elections to the Union itself
rationale: Continues the discussion of the elections clause quoted in the previous paper, naming the power it gives the Union as "the ultimate right of regulating its own elections."

from_quote: The House of Representatives being to be elected immediately by the people
rationale: States that the House of Representatives is "to be elected immediately by the people," the mode of choice in this clause.
to_quote: chosen every second Year by the People of the several States

from_quote: the Senate by the State legislatures
rationale: States that the Senate is to be elected "by the State legislatures," the mode of choice in this clause.

from_quote: any regulation of “time and manner,” which is all that is proposed to be submitted to the national government in respect to that body
rationale: Puts "time and manner" in quotation marks as all that is submitted to the national government for the Senate, pointing at the words of this clause and its exception "as to the Places of chusing Senators."
to_quote: except as to the Places of chusing Senators

from_quote: Its authority would be expressly restricted to the regulation of the TIMES, the PLACES, the MANNER of elections.
rationale: Names the authority over elections by repeating in capitals the opening words of this clause: "the TIMES, the PLACES, the MANNER of elections."
to_quote: The Times, Places and Manner of holding Elections
